You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-101 "PDP – Slide out - Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence. The requester mentioned "feel like we refined this one already" — check whether that's actually true from the ticket's own history before treating this as fresh.

I've already read the full integration doc and PRD coverage for Measmerize, verified today (2026-09-03). Your job is to fetch the actual ticket, check its comment/change history for prior refinement, and fill remaining gaps — NOT to re-derive the integration detail below.

CONFIRMED GROUND TRUTH (.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md, .docs/prd/pdp.md §10-11):
- Measmerize is a third-party sizing widget powering TWO surfaces: Find My Size (body-measurement → size recommendation, updates CTA to "Recommended: Size X") and the Size Guide overlay (Measmerize-first, Contentful fallback when no Measmerize data exists, cm/inch toggle lives in the Contentful fallback only). Both point to the same underlying widget.
- INTEGRATION MODE CONFIRMED (2026-07-06): "Modal Integration" is the required path — the PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between Measmerize and the Contentful fallback); Measmerize is inserted via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). No `#measmerize-button` div is used. This is unusually well-specified compared to most tickets in this batch — script injection timing (once, on first mount, deferred behind LCP), SPA navigation handling (`window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU'`), a full custom-event contract (`measmerize.widget.ready` / `.unavailable` / `.recommend` with `event.detail.defaultSize` / `.addToCart`), and defined failure-mode fallbacks are all already documented — say so as a genuine positive finding, not just problems.
- PDP PRD §10 confirms PRD-051/052 are explicitly "removed as not applicable for SFCC" — the Measmerize widget itself owns recommendation-click navigation and Find-My-Size-link suppression; SFCC/PWA does not build that logic. This meaningfully narrows what SFCC-101 actually needs to build (container/DOM/event wiring, not custom recommendation UI).
- ONE GENUINE, NAMED, STILL-OPEN BLOCKING DECISION: consent-gating approach (integration doc §7, item 1) — Zimmermann Privacy/Legal must confirm whether to (a) load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. Explicitly marked "blocking," owner Zimmermann, not resolved as of the doc's last state. This is the one real blocker here — separate from implementation readiness, which is otherwise strong.
- SCOPE QUESTION worth resolving from the ticket itself: the title says "Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA" — does NOT explicitly mention "Size Guide," even though the PRD treats Find My Size and Size Guide as two faces of the same widget/shell. Confirm whether Size Guide is in this ticket's scope, out of scope with its own separate ticket, or a gap nobody's written yet.
- POSSIBLE DE-RISK: SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer" (separate ticket, already merged as PR #67, "Ready for QA") built PDP slide-out tabs recently — check whether it already provides a reusable slide-out shell this ticket could plug Measmerize into, which would be a substantial scope reduction.
- Today is 2026-09-03, real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active), Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is confirmed stale — don't cite it.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket WITH its full comment history: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-101', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=50, expand='changelog'). Specifically check: has this actually been through a prior refinement pass (an existing estimate, a "refined" label, comments from a past refinement session)? Confirm or correct the "feel like we refined this one already" recollection directly — don't just assume it's true or false.
2. Fetch SFCC-736 (jira_get_issue) to check the reusable-shell de-risk question.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size — note the integration doc makes this unusually clear already? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies (04.2 tracker showed Measmerize "fully pending" as of 2026-07-13 — stale, re-check the ticket for a current Figma link)? (5) API/backend dependencies (name the consent-gating decision as the one real blocker)? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (SPA navigation between products, script cleanup on unmount), desktop/mobile, a11y (focus management into/out of the modal, screen-reader behaviour when Measmerize injects third-party HTML you don't control), data (CSP allowlist for static.client.measmerize.com — check overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts already includes it, since that's a Tier 1 file and a real launch-blocking gap if missing) — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- Direct answer to "was this actually refined already?" — with evidence (a prior estimate, a comment, or "no evidence found, treat as fresh")
- The CSP-allowlist check (does contentSecurityPolicy.ts already include the Measmerize domain?)
- The Size-Guide-in-scope-or-not question, stated directly
- The one genuine blocker (consent-gating decision) — named clearly, separate from the otherwise-strong readiness
- The SFCC-736 reusable-shell finding
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

4	import type { IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from 'http';
5	import { randomBytes } from 'crypto';

7	// SFCC-856 — nonce-based `style-src` so Chakra UI's runtime (emotion) style
8	// injection no longer needs a blanket 'unsafe-inline'. helmet 4.6.0's CSP
9	// directive values accept a function of (req, res) => string, invoked once
10	// per request (helmet/dist/middlewares/content-security-policy/index.d.ts),
11	// which is what makes a per-request nonce possible from this file alone —
12	// no change to ssr.js is required, since `contentSecurityPolicy` is already
13	// passed through to `helmet()` there as a plain value and is re-evaluated
14	// per request regardless.
15	//
16	// `res` is always the real Express Response at runtime — this config is
17	// only ever consumed by `helmet()` inside the Express app in ssr.js — but
18	// helmet's own directive-function type only declares the plain Node
19	// `http.ServerResponse` shape (no `.locals`). Widening the function's own
20	// parameter type to include `.locals` would make it a narrower (subtype)
21	// parameter than helmet's declared function type expects, which fails
22	// assignability under `strictFunctionTypes` (tsconfig.json has `strict:
23	// true`) — so the parameter stays typed exactly as the interface declares,
24	// and `.locals` access goes through a single, explained assertion instead.
25	type ResponseWithLocals = ServerResponse & { locals: Record<string, unknown> };
26	
27	const CSP_NONCE_LOCALS_KEY = 'cspNonce';
28	
29	/**
30	 * Returns this request's CSP nonce, generating and caching it on
31	 * `res.locals` the first time it's requested so every directive that needs
32	 * it shares one value for the lifetime of the request. `res.locals` is the
33	 * same object `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`'s SSR render pipeline passes
34	 * straight through as the `locals` prop to `AppConfig`
35	 * (`overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`), which reads this same
36	 * key back off it to configure Chakra/emotion's style-tag cache with a
37	 * matching nonce — again with no ssr.js involvement, since that pass-through
38	 * already happens inside the SDK's own render pipeline.
39	 */
40	const getOrCreateNonce = (res: ServerResponse): string => {
41	  const resWithLocals = res as ResponseWithLocals; // see ResponseWithLocals comment above
42	  const existing = resWithLocals.locals[CSP_NONCE_LOCALS_KEY];
43	  if (typeof existing === 'string') return existing;
44	  const nonce = randomBytes(16).toString('base64');
45	  resWithLocals.locals[CSP_NONCE_LOCALS_KEY] = nonce;
46	  return nonce;
47	};

80	    // combined `style-src`. CSP nonces can only ever apply to <style> ELEMENTS, never to a
81	    // raw inline `style="..."` ATTRIBUTE (there's no way to carry a nonce on an attribute
82	    // value) — but per the CSP3 spec, a nonce present anywhere in `style-src` disables
83	    // `'unsafe-inline'` for *everything* that directive governs, attributes included. A
84	    // combined `style-src` with both a nonce and 'unsafe-inline' therefore silently broke

92	    // downgrade in the first place.

96	    // with `useDefaults: true` and no explicit `style-src` here, helmet 4.6.0 silently injects

116	      // exact string ever changes, recompute via
117	      // `node -e "console.log('sha256-' + require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('<paste the new preventTransition() CSS string>','utf8').digest('base64'))"`.
118	      "'sha256-GNF74DLkXb0fH3ILHgILFjk1ozCF3SNXQ5mQb7WLu/Y='",

615	## ZimmTabs keyboard accessibility fix (2026-08-31)
616	
617	Tim reported: pressing Tab inside an open drawer moves between the active tab and the close
618	icon instead of cycling the other tab headers, and asked for Tab-to-move/Enter-to-activate
619	behaviour. Checked this against the actual spec before changing anything (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 +
620	WAI-ARIA APG's Tabs pattern, both fetched live) rather than assuming either the bug report or a
621	"just make it accessible" reflex fix was right:
622	
623	- **WCAG 2.1.1 doesn't mandate Tab-based navigation for a composite widget** — any keyboard
624	  path satisfies it.
625	- **WAI-ARIA's Tabs pattern is explicit**: `Tab` moves focus into/out of the tablist as a whole
626	  (arrives on the active tab, leaves to the next focusable element outside it — the close icon,
627	  here); Left/Right/Home/End move *within* the tablist. Two activation models exist —
628	  **automatic** (arrow keys switch the panel immediately, no Enter needed) is recommended
629	  specifically "when panel content is not costly to display," which is exactly this case
630	  (static content, no fetch). **Manual** (Enter/Space required) is for the opposite case.
631	- `ZimmTabs` already implemented automatic activation with Left/Right and a roving tabIndex —
632	  the reported "bug" was actually the Tab key behaving per spec. Confirmed with Tim to keep
633	  automatic activation and fix the real, separate gap instead: no `aria-controls`/`id` linking
634	  each tab to its panel, so a screen reader couldn't announce what a tab controls.
635	
636	**Fixed:**
637	- `ZimmTabs`: added `Home`/`End` key support (jump to first/last tab); new required `ariaLabel`
638	  prop (the tablist itself needs an accessible name — no visible on-page label exists for it,
639	  per APG) and `idPrefix` prop, each tab now gets `id={idPrefix}-tab-{tab.id}` and
640	  `aria-controls={idPrefix}-panel`.
641	- `ZimmPdpDrawer`: generates `idPrefix` via React's `useId()` (unique even with the boutique
642	  `ZimmDrawer` also mounted on the same page); its panel now has `id={idPrefix}-panel`,
643	  `aria-labelledby` pointing at the *currently active* tab's id (updates on every switch), and
644	  `tabIndex={0}` — the last one is its own separate APG recommendation (a tabpanel needs to be
645	  in the Tab sequence when its content isn't itself reliably focusable), so `Tab` from the
646	  active tab now lands in the panel content before reaching the close icon.
